transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hello. Um... well, I guess I'm having some issues with... eating. 

Mainly in the evenings. I keep having these nights where I'll, um, I'll buy a family-size takeout order on the way home. And maybe pick up some chips or bakery things from the store, too. And then... I just end up eating most of it myself. It's like I don't even really register how much is gone until later.
When you're eating this food in the evening, do you feel like you can't stop or control how much you're eating?

Um... yes. I suppose so. It's... well, it's hard to explain. 

Once I start, it's like this awful switch flips. I can be sitting there thinking, you know, 'Taylor, just put it away.' But... my hands just keep opening the containers anyway. It almost feels like I'm not the one in charge anymore.
Does this eating behavior in the evenings make you feel upset, embarrassed, or interfere with your daily life in any way?

Um... yes. It does. 

I don't really... I don't have people over to the house anymore. And, um, I used to do some yoga in the evenings, or go out and do a little gardening, but... I've stopped doing that. After it happens, I just... I feel too ashamed to do much of anything.
How often do these evening eating episodes happen? Would you say at least once a week?

Um... yes. At least. 

I... well, I keep a little journal. And when I look back through it, there has barely been a week in the last several months without at least one of those nights. 

Honestly... most weeks, it happens several times.
After these eating episodes, do you ever make yourself vomit, take laxatives, exercise excessively, or fast in order to control your weight or get rid of the calories?
Um... no. No, I don't... I don't do any of that. I've never made myself sick or taken anything like that. I just... no.
During these evening eating episodes, do you find yourself eating much more quickly than you normally would?

Um... yes. I suppose I do. 

I don't really sit down. I just... I stand there at the dining room table, with the boxes and the microwave. And... I eat so fast I barely even taste anything. I'm just... swallowing one bite while I'm already reaching for the next.
During these evening eating episodes, do you feel a sense of loss of control, like you can't stop eating even if you want to?

I... yes. 

It's... hard to explain. Once I start eating, it's like a switch just... flips. I can be standing there thinking, *Taylor, put it away*, but... my hands just keep opening containers. It feels like I'm not even the one in charge anymore. I just can't stop.
During these evening eating episodes, do you find yourself eating until you feel uncomfortably full?

Yes... I do. 

I just... I keep going until my stomach gets really tight. It... it actually hurts. And then I usually just end up sitting very still on the couch for a while. Just... because even trying to walk upstairs feels too uncomfortable.
Do you find yourself eating large amounts of food during these episodes even when you're not physically hungry?

Yes... most of the time, I'm not hungry at all. 

I usually... I might have already had a normal dinner. But later on, I still end up going through the fridge or the pantry shelves. It's just... like the food is something I have to finish.
Has this eating behavior caused you significant distress, or made it harder for you to function at work, at home, or in social situations?

I suppose so... yes. 

I don't really... invite anyone over to the house anymore. And I've stopped doing my normal evening routines. I used to do yoga, or some chores out in the garden, but... I just skip them now. 

I just feel too... ashamed after it happens. It's hard to focus on anything else.
After these eating episodes, do you feel that your self-worth is strongly influenced by your body shape or weight?

I don't... I wouldn't really say that. No. 

I mean, I'm not thrilled with my weight, but... I don't think about it like that. It's more just... being upset about the eating itself. Not my shape.
During these evening eating episodes, do you find yourself eating much more rapidly than you normally would?

Yes... I suppose I do. 

I eat so fast that... I barely even taste anything. I usually just stand there at the dining room table, with the microwave and the boxes around me... and I just... I'm swallowing one bite while I'm already reaching for the next one.
After these eating episodes, do you often feel depressed, guilty, or very upset with yourself?

I don't... I'm not really sure. 

I try not to sit around and dwell on it once it's over. I usually just... clean up the boxes and go to sleep. I don't really focus on how I'm feeling.
Do you often eat alone during these evenings because you're embarrassed about how much you're eating?

Yes... I prefer to be alone. 

I make sure to wait until my husband is asleep... or if we have contractors working on the house, I wait until they're gone. I just... I wouldn't want anyone to see how much I'm eating. Especially since I'm so careful and put together all day at the office. I'd just be... very embarrassed if anyone saw.
